name: Historic Vids
text:
Gerard K. O'Neill, a physicist, proposed the O'Neill Cylinder, a huge rotating space habitat for millions.

Described in his 1976 book "The High Frontier," it features two spinning cylinders to create artificial gravity. These would have cities, rivers, and farms, powered and lit by mirrors.

O'Neill thought these colonies could solve big problems like improving living standards, reducing pollution, managing population growth, finding clean energy, and controlling Earth's temperature, all without harsh measures.
desc: O'Neill cylinder space habitat NASA paintings

name: Syd Mead - Official
text:
Commissioned by Japanese wheel manufacturer RAYS, Syd Mead imagined a new wheel and the world around it: silver cars catching the dawn as partygoers linger above the roadway. The car in the background wears the existing Super Volk wheel; the foreground car carries Mead’s proposal for what might come next.

Syd Mead
RAYS Wheels, 1985
Gouache on board
22½ × 37 in.

On view now:
Syd Mead: Future Pastime
Transamerica Pyramid Annex Gallery, San Francisco
Through December 17, 2026
Wednesday–Sunday, 11am–6pm

More info at http://futurepastime.net
desc: Silver cars at dawn on elevated roadway

name: Mac Rebisz / voyager212 / macspace.bsky.social
text:
I've been rewatching For All Mankind Season 3 lately and I found one scene pretty interesting. It's the one where Dev (billionaire space entrepreneur) is presenting plans for Mars colony, showing some concept artworks. I took a closer look at one of them. 
This part looked very familiar. That's because it was cut out of my concept art for a lunar outpost I made in 2015.  

It still features a logo of Nansen United, one of the imaginary space companies I've created for my Space That Never Was project.
So, just wanted to share a little fun fact, that apparently Nansen United is canon in FAM timeline.
Little edit: no need for any witch hunts, or calling out - I just found it pretty funny to have my habitat design in the show I like. And to be clear - it's always wrong to use someone else's work or parts of it without authorization, but at the same time I know realities of film production, with very tight deadlines, huge amount of work in a stressful environment, where things change really fast and sometimes things like this can slip into production and mistakes are made.
